home.heroTitle: A quiet place to come home to.
home.heroSubtitle: Bodaiju Residences — Japanese-inspired serviced living in the heart of Medini. Foreign-eligible from RM299,000, minutes from the Second Link, LEGOLAND, EduCity and Gleneagles.
home.heroByline: By Creed Group (Japan) · Built by MGB Berhad · Completion 2028
home.conceptTitle: Named for the tree of stillness and growth
home.conceptBody: The Bodhi Tree — a symbol of enlightenment, peace, longevity and growth. That philosophy shapes everything here — sky gardens, green courtyards and Japanese-considered spaces designed to let modern life slow down, even at the edge of one of Southeast Asia's fastest-growing corridors.
home.trustEyebrow: Why you can take this seriously
home.trust1Body: Creed Group (Japan, est. 1996) completed a 928-unit Bodaiju in Phnom Penh in 2020 — a real, occupied precedent at this exact scale.
home.trust2Body: A Bursa-disclosed contract with listed builder MGB Construction & Engineering. Tower A targets completion by 30 Nov 2027.
home.trust3Body: Creed is a privately-held Japanese investor — financially unrelated to Country Garden / Forest City.
home.absdBody1: A foreigner buying residential property in Singapore pays 60% Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty — before the price of the home itself.
home.absdBody2: Here, the same budget buys a brand-new 1-bedroom serviced residence in Medini — with no minimum-price barrier for foreigners.
home.absdAllIn: All-in upfront as a foreign buyer ≈
home.absdDisclaimer: Illustrative. Includes 8% stamp duty, state consent & legal fees. Confirm with your solicitor.
home.sellingTitle: Eight reasons that hold up to scrutiny
home.residencesDisclaimer: Indicative prices, subject to unit, level and availability. Per-floor pricing confirmed on enquiry.
home.locationTitle: Quiet by nature. Connected by design.
home.locationBody: Medini sits inside the Johor–Singapore Special Economic Zone, with the RTS Link arriving in 2027. You're 9 km from the Second Link and steps from daily life.
home.transparencyTitle: We publish what we can verify — and flag what we can't
home.transparencyBody: Cross-border property has real risks: tenure structure, oversupply, currency, delivery. We don't bury them. Every claim here is sourced, and the items still awaiting the developer's written confirmation are listed openly.
home.finalTitle: Start with the numbers, not the sales pitch.
home.finalBody: See exactly what a Bodaiju home costs you — all-in, in ringgit and Singapore dollars — before you speak to anyone.

units.heroTitle: Four ways to live at Bodaiju
units.heroSubtitle: From an efficient one-bedroom to a dual-key three-bedroom, every layout is designed around the Japanese principle of Ma — meaningful, unhurried space. All units include a balcony.
units.disclaimer: Prices are indicative starting prices, subject to unit, level, orientation and availability. Built-up areas are approximate. Refer to the Sale and Purchase Agreement for final specifications.

calculator.heroTitle: What a Bodaiju home really costs you
calculator.heroSubtitle: Most listings show you RM299,000 and stop there. This shows the full picture — stamp duty, state consent, legal fees and monthly repayment — in ringgit and Singapore dollars. No surprises at the lawyer's office.
calculator.priceSliderNote: Base price is {price}. Slide up to estimate higher floors / better views.
calculator.upfrontExplain: Includes your {pct} down payment (equity you keep) plus ~{txn} in transaction costs (stamp duty, {extra}legal fees).
calculator.absdLine: In Singapore, a foreigner would pay {amount} in 60% ABSD alone on this sum — before the price of any home. Here, it buys the whole unit.
calculator.sendEstimate: Send this estimate to our team
calculator.calcDisclaimer: Calculator figures are estimates for general guidance only, based on stated assumptions and current tax rates. They are not a quotation or financial advice. Confirm all figures with your solicitor and bank before transacting.
calculator.howWeCalcBody: Foreign buyers pay a flat 8% Memorandum of Transfer stamp duty (effective 1 January 2026), plus Johor state consent (≈3% or RM30,000, whichever is higher), 0.5% loan stamp duty and ~1.5% legal fees. Malaysian citizens pay tiered MOT stamp duty (1–4%) with no state consent. Monthly repayment assumes ~3.85% p.a. over 30 years at the indicated loan-to-value. All figures are estimates — confirm with your solicitor and bank.
